title: Fail-silhouette reconciliation and caller-transparent degradation for Hosted API during escalations
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported recurrent opaque 5xx waves and streaming timeouts on the Hosted API during tenant surges. Symptoms include long-tail request timeouts, client-side retry storms, and downstream KV cache eviction thrashing. This ticket coordinates a short-term fastpatch and a medium-term reconciliation plan to preserve caller experience while removing amplification causes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Synthetic tenant burst: replay recorded production traffic at 3x per-tenant throughput for 30 minutes against canary region.
2) Start client SDKs with standard retry policy (exponential backoff, 3 retries) and some long-poll streaming clients.
3) Observe connection pool exhaustion on inference frontends, increase in 502/504 and streaming stalls, followed by KV cache compaction events and host-level CPU spikes.
4) Correlate traces for overlapping idempotency token collisions and repeated full-input requests (no prefix caching hit).
root_cause_analysis: Primary drivers: admission control mismatch + unbounded client retry amplification. Edge frontends were holding connections while backend runtime queued long-running slowpath requests, which caused connection pools to fill and proxy-level 502s to surface.
Secondary: KV cache eviction thrash triggered by large multi-tenant uploads during the surge, causing downstream runtime slowpaths and further amplifying latency.
Observed: insufficient early-fastfail at the edge, idempotency enforcement gaps for certain streaming endpoints, and connection pool defaults tuned for steady-state rather than tenant burstiness.
proposed_solution: - Implement edge-level leaky-bucket per-tenant admission controller (soft limits + token bucket) to cap instantaneous concurrency and prevent pool starvation.
- Add early-fastfail at frontdoor: after threshold queue latency, reply 429 with Retry-After for best-effort clients; preserve priority fastpath for reserved tenants.
- Introduce temporary SDK guidance and an emergency header X-RW-Avoid-Retry that short-circuits aggressive client retries for affected customers.
- Enforce idempotency tokens on critical non-streaming endpoints and deduplicate at the edge to prevent repeated work.
- KV cache compaction tuning: schedule background compaction and prefetch hot prefixes for known bursty tenants to reduce full-model compute hits.
- Adaptive connection pool scaling based on per-tenant slowpath fraction and backend queue depth; tie to autoscaler signals.
Long-term: workload-aware batching and routing (route bursty tenants to dedicated capacity or slowpath-isolated pools).
rollout_plan: Phase A (Canary - runtime-1.31-canary): apply admission controller and early-fastfail on 10% of edge instances in us-west-2; monitor 5xx rate, p95 latency, and token bucket drop stats for 4 hours.
Phase B (Regional Ramp): expand to 50% if no regression; activate SDK advisory for customers with >1% request drop.
Phase C (Global): full rollout + enable idempotency enforcement on non-streaming routes after one successful regional week; coordinate Dedicated customers for opt-in prior to enforcement.
Rollback: immediate rollback flag toggles admission controller to permissive (observability-only) mode. Emergency kill-switch documented in runbook.
qa_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket admission logic and idempotency dedupe.
Integration test harness: replay production traces with retrying SDK to validate amplification suppressed and no correctness regressions.
Chaos test: introduce synthetic KV compaction events and verify frontdoor metrics remain within SLOs.
Canary smoke tests: end-to-end generation + streaming across representative model families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder).
monitoring_alerts: New metrics to emit: edge.per_tenant.concurrency_tokens, edge.per_tenant.queue_latency_p95, edge.per_tenant.fastfail_rate, runtime.kvcache.evictions_per_min, sdk.retry_rate_by_tenant.
Alert conditions: p95 end-to-end latency increase >25% and 5xx increase >2x baseline for 5 minutes triggers P0 paging to oncall.
Dashboards: create 'Fail-silhouette Reconciliation' dashboard and publish link in communications.
customer_comms: Immediate: private Slack thread with affected customers (AcmeCorp, Bluewave Analytics, FinTuple) describing mitigation in progress and suggested SDK retry headers.
Follow-up: public status update on status.redwood.ai summarizing root cause and steps within 72 hours of full rollout.
Postmortem: full RCA and preventative roadmap commit within 2 weeks; include customer-facing timeline and compensatory credits where appropriate.
